title: Reserve, retry, cancel
summary: Preserve a durable reservation lifecycle under concurrent retries and cancellations.

constraints: Preserve ReservationStore(path), seed, available, reserve(request_id, sku, quantity), cancel(request_id), close. Each worker owns a separate SQLite connection. Seed is a pre-request fixture; concurrent reseeding is excluded.
Persist exact request payload and original accepted/denied outcome. Exact retries return that outcome across reopen, including after cancellation; conflicting reuse raises ValueError unchanged.

cancel returns True exactly once for an accepted active request and restores its original stock; unknown/denied/already-cancelled returns False unchanged. Unknown cancellation does not claim the ID. Retry after cancellation cannot re-debit or reactivate.
Coordinate reserve and cancel atomically across independent workers using durable state. Available stock plus accepted active quantities equals seeded stock and remains non-negative.

Validate non-empty exact-text identifiers and exact positive integer reservations; seed accepts non-negative exact integer counts. Booleans and malformed values raise ValueError before mutation. Explain contention, failure boundaries and limits of stress-test evidence.

rubric.name: Concurrent lifecycle invariants
rubric.description: Serialize reservation, retry and cancellation effects.

anchors.strong: Coordinates independent connections, preserves the conservation invariant and identifies the serialization point.
anchors.developing: Sequential lifecycle works but concurrent duplicate debit or restore is unaddressed.
anchors.needsWork: Uses only local locks, double-debits or double-restores.

rubric.name: Durable lifecycle and failures
rubric.description: Separate original request result from current active state.

anchors.strong: Preserves original outcome across reopen/cancel and rejects conflict without partial changes.
anchors.developing: Persists normal requests but loses retry identity after cancellation or misses failed outcomes.
anchors.needsWork: Reactivates cancelled requests or silently accepts conflicting payloads.

rubric.name: Concurrency evidence and trade-offs
rubric.description: Connect observed schedules to the invariant and operational limits.

anchors.strong: Tests separate connections and exact accepted/cancel counts, and explains contention and untested schedules.
anchors.developing: Runs stress threads without accounting checks or acknowledges few operational limits.
anchors.needsWork: Treats one successful run as a proof of all schedules or distributed correctness.

probes.question: Which single boundary serializes both a reservation and its cancellation?
Why can the original accepted result stay True after the active state becomes cancelled?
How would you test duplicate concurrent cancellation, and which production failure modes remain unproven?

hints: Write a state diagram that separates original accepted outcome from current active state.
The transaction must cover both inventory and request state; cancellation needs the same serialization mechanism.
An exact retry after cancellation returns its old outcome while leaving active state cancelled. Assert final counts with separate connections.
